headline: Oil tops $90 and PSX blinks — a near-2,000-point morning slide, clawed back to a 125-point green close.
summary: Brent crude topped $90/bbl this weekend as US-Iran strikes entered a ninth night, and PSX opened almost 2,000 points lower today before bulls clawed most of it back to close up 124.95 points. SBP reserves have slipped to $17.2bn and the government is weighing austerity again, keeping the rupee and import bill under strain. Regime stays risk-off: the desk leans toward E&P, banks and fertilizer (oil windfall, high-rate carry, defensive demand) and away from OMCs, autos, cement and textile exporters (import-cost and current-account exposure). New setups stay capped at two favoured-sector names until the tape settles.

sectors.name: Banks
sectors.why: High-rate carry and sub-policy-rate T-bill funding costs still support margins, though the sector was Friday's single worst performer as bank-heavy selling led the last confirmed sell-off.

sectors.name: E&P
sectors.why: Brent above $90 on the Strait-of-Hormuz standoff is a direct revenue tailwind for OGDC/PPL/MARI/POL, even though the same headlines can trigger the index-wide risk-off selling that drags E&P down with everything else.

sectors.name: Fertilizer
sectors.why: Domestic-demand defensive with low direct oil-import exposure; FFC and EFERT both report results within the next ten days.

sectors.name: OMCs
sectors.why: A wider import bill and slipping forex reserves ($17.2bn, -6.7% WoW) squeeze an already thin-margin business carrying circular-debt risk.

sectors.name: Autos
sectors.why: Imported-input costs and an inflation-squeezed consumer are a bad combination while the rupee is under renewed pressure.

sectors.name: Cement
sectors.why: Energy-cost sensitive names were among the hardest hit in this month's Commercial Banks/E&P/Cement-led sell-offs.

sectors.name: Textile exporters
sectors.why: FY26 exports basically flatlined (+0.26% YoY) and June alone fell almost 17% YoY, with Gulf shipping-route risk layered on top while Hormuz tension persists.

watchlist.angle: The only live technical trigger in a favoured sector today: the desk's signal feed flags a fresh 'Volume leads price' (OBV accumulation) setup with a 97% historical hit rate over 89 backtested trades and an 83% out-of-sample hit rate — high confidence by the desk's own rules. Stacks with an 'attractive' fundamental read (cheap P/E 6.62, 32% net margin) and a results date pencilled for 2026-07-31.
watchlist.risk: No dividend cushion, and Commercial Banks were Friday's worst-performing sector (-680 index points) — a return of broad bank-sector selling on fresh Hormuz headlines would swamp the technical signal.

watchlist.angle: Best price momentum of the big banks right now — above both its 20- and 50-day averages with RSI 57.6 and a +6% 20-day return even as the sector wobbled. UBL's own backtest history shows its 'MACD reclaims zero' and 'Consolidation break' setups net roughly 2.7% and 2.2% per trade with 74-76% hit rates. Fundamentals screen 'attractive' (cheap, 30% net margin, 6.87% covered yield), and results land within days (pencilled 2026-07-22, unconfirmed).
watchlist.risk: That earnings date is very close — a NIM miss, with T-bill cutoffs already pricing a rate cut, could reverse the momentum fast.

watchlist.angle: The one E&P name still holding its trend while OGDC, PPL and MARI all broke below their 50-day averages this week — POL sits within 2.5% of its 20-day high. Its 'Trend strength turning up' setup has netted about 1.9% per trade on POL's own history (68% hit rate, 63% out-of-sample). Fundamentals are the cleanest in the sector too: cheap P/E 7.1, 48% net margin, an 11% dividend yield covered at an 80% payout. Results are dated for 2026-08-11.
watchlist.risk: E&P is a two-edged Brent trade — the same Strait-of-Hormuz spike that lifts POL's revenue is exactly what triggered the >6,000-point single-day PSX plunges earlier this month; a risk-off wave drags E&P down with everything else regardless of the chart.

catalysts.event: UBL and BWCL Q2 results (scraped estimate, unconfirmed)
DCR and LOTCHEM go ex-dividend (6.6% final / 15% interim, both confirmed)
SBP MPC — first FY27 rate decision; 6M/12M T-bill cutoffs already sit below the policy rate, pricing a cut
FFC and EFERT results (scraped estimate, unconfirmed)
BAFL and BML results (scraped estimate, unconfirmed)

risks: Brent is still climbing on a ninth straight night of US-Iran strikes — any further escalation (a real Strait closure, a direct hit on Gulf energy infrastructure) would hit PKR and the import bill fast, the same dynamic behind this month's >6,000-point single-day plunges.

SBP reserves fell 6.7% w/w to $17.2bn and the government is reportedly weighing reactivating austerity measures — a reserve/balance-of-payments scare has been the trigger for sharp PSX sell-offs before.
SBP's July 27 MPC is a coin-flip event: T-bill cutoffs already price in a cut, so a hawkish hold could jolt both banks and the broader index right after this read is published.
